My research focuses on **bias-robust Bayesian evidence synthesis**,
especially for applied literatures where published findings are noisy,
selective, and difficult to interpret. I am particularly interested in
publication bias, meta-analysis, nutrition and health evidence, and
reproducible statistical workflows.

## Research interests

- **Bias-robust Bayesian meta-analysis.**
  RoBMA, model-averaged Bayes factors, selection models, heterogeneity,
  and evidence for or against effects after accounting for bias.

- **Publication bias and evidential fragility.**
  Selective reporting, small-study effects, threshold behavior, and how
  these distort applied literatures.

- **Nutrition and health evidence synthesis.**
  Applying bias-aware Bayesian methods to intervention meta-analyses in
  nutrition, fitness, and health.

- **Reproducible statistical workflows.**
  R, Quarto, Git, simulation studies, public repositories, and
  transparent research pipelines.

- **Statistics education.**
  Introductory statistics, Bayesian intuition, reproducible work, and
  AI-supported mathematical/statistical learning.

## Projects

### Bias-robust Bayesian reanalysis of nutrition intervention meta-analyses

Reanalyzing published nutrition intervention meta-analyses with
bias-aware Bayesian model averaging, to characterize how much
selective reporting and small-study effects move the conclusions.

### Rigor and attenuation in evidence synthesis

Studying how methodological rigor — design, blinding, reporting,
preregistration — interacts with bias correction and effect-size
attenuation in applied literatures.

### Reproducible research and teaching infrastructure

Building durable Quarto + R + Git pipelines for both research analyses
and the public-facing course sites at
[`/math-software/`](/math-software/) and
[`/intro-stats/`](/intro-stats/).

### Bayesian statistics education

Materials and exploratory work on how to bring Bayesian intuition into
introductory statistics, and on the responsible use of AI assistants
in mathematical and statistical learning.
